entities.name: Ketone reduction
observations: The encoded net transformation changes a ketone carbonyl, [C](=O)[C], into a secondary alcohol, [C](O)[C], while retaining the rest of the scaffold.
If the two ketone substituents differ, reduction creates a new stereocenter and may produce racemic or diastereomeric products.
No clean exact-substrate reaction precedent was identified in the local reaction database; unrelated C–C bond-forming records should not be treated as condition matches.

entities.name: NaBH4 ketone reduction
observations: Sodium borohydride, commonly in methanol or ethanol, is a reasonable first-screen reagent because it is mild and commonly reduces ketones selectively.
Chemoselectivity should be checked against aldehydes, imines, N-oxides, activated alkenes, esters, amides, and reducible heteroaromatic groups.

entities.name: Alternative hydride reduction
observations: LiBH4 or borane may be considered when sodium borohydride is insufficient, but they can have broader functional-group reactivity.
LiAlH4 is generally unnecessarily aggressive for a simple ketone; DIBAL-H is less attractive because of sensitivity and possible over-reduction.
K-selectride or L-selectride may be considered when stereoselective reduction is needed.
